items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And of course he had Ivy then. And he loved Ivy. Ivy to me was not the singer that Billie was or one or two people. But she was a stylist, and she could fit right in there, what Duke wanted.

ctx.x: That they sold. Well let’s say better what were the big things in the stage shows. Because you know at the stage shows the screen would come on and the medley would come on, you couldn’t help it. It had to be, you know, because that’s what the public knew. And so you had “Sophisticated Lady,” and you had all the things. And when you’d get rid of the medley, then you’d see what Ellington was going to give you, you know. He changed that quite a bit. And of course then he would have to have a vocalist. But of course…

those things, and Rex would play those things in the background you know, “Rug Cutter” and those things, and well no, Sonny did those funny things with Ivy, but Rex too, on the horn. And so I don’t know whether I’ve answered your question properly.
